correctness.rationale: The semidirect images respect all six defining relations. Independently, each relation swaps one of the six unordered distinct coordinate-increment pairs at the identity, and a prefix with permutation p transports that swap by p. Each ordered increment list decodes to a unique word, so adjacent swaps identify exactly words with the same nonnegative translation coordinate. The word x_0^2 x_1 x_3 gives the central translation q=(1,1,1,1), and the increment argument expresses it with any x_i first. Thus every x_i inverse is a positive word times q inverse, giving first-coordinate existence and uniqueness on the fraction group by translating far enough by q. In particular left translation cosets of N correspond to coordinate cosets and its index is eight; this fills the index step explicitly. The four stated translation vectors satisfy the congruences and have determinant of magnitude eight, and the congruence map onto Z/2 × Z/4 is surjective. Thus N is precisely Lambda. Conjugation by its full-rank translation subgroup gives infinite classes for elements with nonidentity permutation and finite F-orbits for translations. Finite-support central elements have constant coefficients on conjugacy classes in every characteristic; commuting with the monoid generators implies commuting with their inverses in the group algebra. This gives the stated positive-support center. The exact independent script /workspace/review-work/algebra_check.py verifies the local swaps, translation vectors, all eight fixed-vector residue polynomials by cross-multiplication, and their Burnside sum numerator 8(1-t^2+t^4) over the common denominator. Hence the series is an infinite rational identity and remains characteristic-independent, not merely a degree-sixteen fit.
residual_risks: The conclusion is for the coefficient-free presentation. Dihedral describes the finite holonomy, not the infinite fraction group; the wording 'dihedral group of fractions' in the frozen prior-work paragraph should be read with this distinction.
